### Load packages and data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(glmnet)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(flextable)


# Load the merged TPM dataset
analysis_tpm <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "analysis_tpm.rds"))

# Check dimensions
dim(analysis_tpm)

```

### Separate the outcome and predictors

```{r}

# Identify gene columns 
gene_cols <- grep(
  "^ENSG",
  names(analysis_tpm),
  value = TRUE
)

# Extract gene expression matrix
X_mat <- as.matrix(analysis_tpm[, gene_cols])

# Transform TPM values
X_mat <- log2(X_mat + 1)


# Primary outcome = natural-log-transformed plasmablast frequency
stopifnot(all(y_vec > 0))
y_log <- log(y_vec)

# check dimensions
dim(X_mat)
length(y_vec)
```

We transform the TPM values using log2(TPM+1) because RNA-seq gene expression is typically highly skewed since many genes have low expression and only a small number have high expression.

The transformation compresses large values.

### Check the data

```{r}
# Confirm predictor and outcome dimensions match
stopifnot(nrow(X_mat)== length(y_vec))

# Check for missing values
sum(is.na(X_mat))
sum(is.na(y_vec))

# Check for infinite values
sum(!is.finite(X_mat))

# Summarize outcome
summary(y_vec)
```

### Check gene-expression variability

```{r}
# Calculate the variance of each gene across participants
gene_variances <- apply(X_mat, 2, var)

# Count genes with zero and nonzero variance
sum(gene_variances == 0)
sum(gene_variances > 0)

# Summarize gene variances
summary(gene_variances)
```

A substantial proportion of genes have no variation in expression across the 29 participants (25213) meaning these cannot help the elastic net model distinguish between individuals.

-   Total genes = 78,932

-   Zero-variance genes = 25,213 (31.9%)

-   Nonzero-variance genes = 53,719 (68.1%) (Genes whose expression differs between at least two participants)

Variance here is calculated after transforming expression values using log(TPM+1)

For the final predictive analysis we will have to perform gene filtering within the cross-validation training folds to avoid information leakage. Nonzero variance alone also does not mean that a gene is predictive of plasmablast frequency.

don't remove the 25,213 genes from the entire dataset yet. Instead, we filter genes separately within each training fold, so the held-out participants don't influence preprocessing

### Elastic net regression with nested cross-validation

```{r}

set.seed(123)
# Create five outer folds for model evaluation
folds <- createFolds(
  y_vec,
  k = 5,
  list = TRUE
)

# Check number of participants in each test fold
sapply(folds, length)
```

**Outer cross-validation:** Divides the 29 participants into five groups. Each group serves as the test set once, while the remaining participants are used for training.

**Inner cross-validation:** In each outer training set, we use another five-fold cross-validation procedure to select the optimal α and λ

### Fit elastic net using nested cross-validation (not transformed)

```{r}

# Nested cross-validation: elastic net

# Using the tuning grid and outer folds created above

elastic_net_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
  lambda = c(
    0.000001,
    0.00001,
    0.0001,
    0.001,
    0.01,
    0.05,
    0.1
  )
)

# Create vectors for storing results
elastic_net_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vec))
baseline_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vec))

best_alphas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
best_lambdas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
genes_retained <- rep(NA_integer_, length(folds))

# Calculate RMSE only during inner cross-validation
rmse_only <- function(data, lev = NULL, model = NULL) {
  c(RMSE = sqrt(mean((data$obs - data$pred)^2)))
}

# Repeat across all five outer folds
for (i in seq_along(folds)) {

  cat("Running outer fold", i, "\n")

  # Select held-out participants
  test_idx <- folds[[i]]

  # Divide data into training and testing sets
  X_train <- X_mat[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test  <- X_mat[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  y_train <- y_vec[-test_idx]

  # Identify genes with nonzero variance in training data
  keep_genes <- apply(X_train, 2, var) > 0

  # Keep the same gene columns in training and testing sets
  X_train <- X_train[, keep_genes, drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_test[, keep_genes, drop = FALSE]

  genes_retained[i] <- sum(keep_genes)

  # Inner cross-validation selects alpha and lambda
  elastic_net_model <- caret::train(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    method = "glmnet",
    tuneGrid = elastic_net_grid,
    trControl = trainControl(
      method = "cv",
      number = 5,
      summaryFunction = rmse_only
    ),
    metric = "RMSE",
    preProcess = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
    standardize = FALSE
  )

  # Predict participants in the held-out outer fold
  elastic_net_predictions[test_idx] <- as.numeric(
    predict(elastic_net_model, newdata = X_test)
  )

  # Simple reference model: training-set mean outcome
  baseline_predictions[test_idx] <- mean(y_train)

  # Store selected tuning parameters
  best_alphas[i] <- elastic_net_model$bestTune$alpha
  best_lambdas[i] <- elastic_net_model$bestTune$lambda
}

# Confirm all participants have a prediction
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(elastic_net_predictions),
  !anyNA(baseline_predictions)
)

```

#### Evaluate elastic net (not transformed)

```{r}

# RMSE: average magnitude of prediction errors
rmse_elastic_net <- sqrt(
  mean((y_vec - elastic_net_predictions)^2)
)

# Pooled cross-validated R-squared
r2_elastic_net <- 1 -
  sum((y_vec - elastic_net_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2)

# Compare with a simple baseline model
rmse_baseline <- sqrt(
  mean((y_vec - baseline_predictions)^2)
)

r2_baseline <- 1 -
  sum((y_vec - baseline_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2)

# show results
data.frame(
  model = c("Elastic net", "Training-mean baseline"),
  RMSE = c(rmse_elastic_net, rmse_baseline),
  R2 = c(r2_elastic_net, r2_baseline)
)

# look at selected hyperparameters and retained genes
data.frame(
  fold = seq_along(folds),
  alpha = best_alphas,
  lambda = best_lambdas,
  genes_retained = genes_retained
)



```

RMSE = lower is better

baseline model is extremely simple. it doesn't use gene expression at all and just predicts the average plasmablast frequency of the training participants (just a simple average)

R^2^ = 1 is perfect prediction, R^2^ = 0 means predictions are as good as the overall sample mean, and R\^2 below 0 means predictions are worse than that overall-mean benchmark

-   **Small lambda:** The model is allowed to rely more strongly on gene expression patterns.

-   **Large lambda:** The model shrinks the gene coefficients more heavily, making its predictions less dependent on those patterns.

### Additional analyses

## Combined elastic net model with baseline gene expression + age + sex (not transformed outcome)

```{r}

# Combined elastic net: gene expression + demographics

# Create numeric demographic predictors
# model.matrix() converts biological_sex into a dummy variable
demographic_mat <- model.matrix(
  ~ age + biological_sex,
  data = analysis_tpm
)[, -1, drop = FALSE]

# Combine gene expression with demographic predictors
X_combined <- cbind(
  X_mat,
  demographic_mat
)

# Check dimensions
dim(X_combined)

# Check demographic variable names
colnames(demographic_mat)

# Confirm rows match the outcome
stopifnot(
  nrow(X_combined) == length(y_vec),
  !anyNA(X_combined),
  all(is.finite(X_combined))
)

```

### Fit the combined elastic net (not transformed outcome)

```{r}

# Store predictions for each participant
combined_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vec))

# Store the best tuning parameters
combined_alphas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
combined_lambdas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
combined_genes_retained <- rep(NA_integer_, length(folds))

# Reuse the SAME outer folds and tuning grid
for (i in seq_along(folds)) {

  cat("Running combined model - outer fold", i, "\n")

  # 1. Select held-out participants
  test_idx <- folds[[i]]

  # 2. Split training and testing data
  X_train <- X_combined[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test  <- X_combined[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  y_train <- y_vec[-test_idx]

  # 3. Remove zero-variance predictors using training data
  keep_predictors <- apply(X_train, 2, var) > 0

  X_train <- X_train[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]
  X_test  <- X_test[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]

  combined_genes_retained[i] <- sum(
    keep_predictors[seq_len(ncol(X_mat))]
  )

  # 4. Tune alpha and lambda using inner cross-validation
  combined_model <- caret::train(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    method = "glmnet",
    tuneGrid = elastic_net_grid,
    trControl = trainControl(
      method = "cv",
      number = 5,
      summaryFunction = rmse_only
    ),
    metric = "RMSE",
    preProcess = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
    standardize = FALSE
  )

  # 5. Predict held-out participants
  combined_predictions[test_idx] <- as.numeric(
    predict(combined_model, newdata = X_test)
  )

  # 6. Store selected parameters
  combined_alphas[i] <- combined_model$bestTune$alpha
  combined_lambdas[i] <- combined_model$bestTune$lambda
}

# Check that all 29 participants received predictions
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(combined_predictions),
  all(is.finite(combined_predictions))
)

```

### RMSE and R\^2 (non-transformed outcome)

```{r}

# RMSE for combined model
rmse_combined <- sqrt(
  mean((y_vec - combined_predictions)^2)
)

# Cross-validated R-squared
r2_combined <- 1 -
  sum((y_vec - combined_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2)

# Compare all four models
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Mean-only baseline (non-transformed)",
    "Gene-expression elastic net (non-transformed)",
    "Combined elastic net (non-transformed)"
  ),
  RMSE = c(
    rmse_baseline,
    rmse_elastic_net,
    rmse_combined
  ),
  R2 = c(
    r2_baseline,
    r2_elastic_net,
    r2_combined
  )
)

model_comparison

# Selected alpha and lambda in each outer fold
data.frame(
  fold = seq_along(folds),
  alpha = combined_alphas,
  lambda = combined_lambdas,
  genes_retained = combined_genes_retained
)


```

The gene-expression-only model performed best, although its advantage over the mean-only baseline was extremely small.

The combined model performed worse than both gene expression alone and the mean-only baseline.

#### Fit the elastic net using this log-transformed outcome

```{r}
# Store predictions and selected hyperparameters
log_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vec))

log_alphas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
log_lambdas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
# Wider lambda grid for the log-transformed outcome
# log_elastic_net_grid <- expand.grid(
#   alpha = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
#   lambda = c(
#     0.000001,
#     0.00001,
#     0.0001,
#     0.001,
#     0.01,
#     0.05,
#     0.1,
#     0.2,
#     0.5,
#     1
#   )
# )

log_elastic_net_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha  = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
  lambda = 10^seq(-3, 4, length.out = 30)   # 0.001 to 10,000
)

for (i in seq_along(folds)) {
  cat("Running log-transformed model - outer fold", i, "\n")

  test_idx <- folds[[i]]

  # Split expression data
  X_train <- X_mat[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_mat[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  # Use log-transformed outcome
  y_train <- y_log[-test_idx]

  # Remove zero-variance genes using training data only
  keep_genes <- apply(X_train, 2, var) > 0

  X_train <- X_train[, keep_genes, drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_test[, keep_genes, drop = FALSE]

  # Fit elastic net with inner 5-fold CV
  log_model <- caret::train(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    method = "glmnet",
    tuneGrid = log_elastic_net_grid,
    trControl = trainControl(
      method = "cv",
      number = 5,
      summaryFunction = rmse_only
    ),
    metric = "RMSE",
    preProcess = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
    standardize = FALSE
  )

  # Predict on log scale and back-transform
  pred_log <- predict(log_model, newdata = X_test)

  log_predictions[test_idx] <- exp(pred_log)

  # Save selected parameters
  log_alphas[i] <- log_model$bestTune$alpha
  log_lambdas[i] <- log_model$bestTune$lambda
}
```

#### Compare predictive performance

```{r}
# Performance on original outcome scale
log_rmse <- sqrt(mean((y_vec - log_predictions)^2))

log_r2 <- 1 -
  sum((y_vec - log_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2)

# Compare models
data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Original outcome",
    "Log-transformed outcome"
  ),
  RMSE = c(
    sqrt(mean((y_vec - elastic_net_predictions)^2)),
    log_rmse
  ),
  R2 = c(
    1 - sum((y_vec - elastic_net_predictions)^2) /
      sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2),
    log_r2
  )
)

data.frame(
  Fold = seq_along(folds),
  Alpha = log_alphas,
  Lambda = log_lambdas
)
```

## Log-transformed outcome, run one chunk to compare all of the 4 models (baseline, gene expression, genes + age + sex, genes + age + sex + vaccines) = main model reported

```{r}
# Log-transformed outcome: comparison of four models

# Outcome
stopifnot(all(y_vec > 0))
y_log <- log(y_vec)

# Missing vaccination histories must be NA, not zero
vax_count <- analysis_tpm$n_prior_vax
vax_count[!vax_available] <- NA_real_

# Reuse existing gene-expression matrix
# X_mat already contains log2(TPM + 1)

# Gene expression + age + sex
X_log_demographic <- X_combined

# Expanded grid for log-transformed outcome
log_elastic_net_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
  lambda = c(
    0.000001, 0.00001, 0.0001,
    0.001, 0.01, 0.05,
    0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1,
    2, 5, 10, 20
  )
)

# Define model predictor sets
log_models <- list(
  "Gene expression" = X_mat,
  "Genes + age + sex" = X_log_demographic,
  "Genes + age + sex + vaccination history" = X_log_demographic
)
```

```{r}
# Store held-out predictions on the LOG scale
log_model_predictions <- list()

# Store tuning parameters
log_model_tuning <- list()

# Baseline model: training-set mean of log outcome
log_baseline_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_log))

for (i in seq_along(folds)) {

  test_idx <- folds[[i]]

  log_baseline_predictions[test_idx] <- mean(y_log[-test_idx])
}

log_model_predictions[["Training-mean baseline"]] <-
  log_baseline_predictions


# Fit the three elastic net models
for (model_name in names(log_models)) {

  cat("\nRunning:", model_name, "\n")

  X_current <- log_models[[model_name]]

  predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_log))

  tuning <- data.frame(
    Fold = seq_along(folds),
    Alpha = NA_real_,
    Lambda = NA_real_
  )

  for (i in seq_along(folds)) {

    cat("Outer fold", i, "\n")

    test_idx <- folds[[i]]

    X_train <- X_current[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    X_test <- X_current[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

    y_train <- y_log[-test_idx]

    # Add vaccination history only for the third model
    if (model_name == "Genes + age + sex + vaccination history") {
      # Keep missing values as NA
      # caret will impute them within each inner training fold
      
      median_impute <- function(X_train, X_test) {
        na_cols <- which(colSums(is.na(X_train)) > 0 | colSums(is.na(X_test)) > 0)
      
        for (j in na_cols) {
          med <- median(X_train[, j], na.rm = TRUE)
          X_train[is.na(X_train[, j]), j] <- med
          X_test[is.na(X_test[, j]), j]   <- med
        }
      
        list(train = X_train, test = X_test)
      }
    }
    
    imp     <- median_impute(X_train, X_test)
    X_train <- imp$train
    X_test  <- imp$test
    

        # Identify nonzero-variance predictors using outer training data
    # na.rm = TRUE allows the vaccination variable to contain NA
    keep_predictors <- apply(
      X_train,
      2,
      function(x) {
        v <- var(x, na.rm = TRUE)
        is.finite(v) && v > 0
      }
    )
    
    X_train <- X_train[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]
    X_test <- X_test[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]
    
    # Median imputation is required only for the vaccination model
    if (model_name ==
        "Genes + age + sex + vaccination history") {
    
      preprocessing <- c("zv", "center", "scale")
    
    } else {
    
      preprocessing <- c("zv", "center", "scale")
    }

    # Use the same inner CV splits for each model
    set.seed(1000 + i)

    inner_folds <- createFolds(
      y_train,
      k = 5,
      returnTrain = TRUE
    )

    # Fit elastic net
    model <- caret::train(
      x = X_train,
      y = y_train,
      method = "glmnet",
      tuneGrid = log_elastic_net_grid,
      trControl = trainControl(
        method = "cv",
        index = inner_folds,
        summaryFunction = rmse_only
      ),
      metric = "RMSE",
      preProcess = preprocessing,
      standardize = FALSE
    )

    # Held-out predictions on log scale
    predictions[test_idx] <- as.numeric(
      predict(model, newdata = X_test)
    )

    tuning$Alpha[i] <- model$bestTune$alpha
    tuning$Lambda[i] <- model$bestTune$lambda
  }

  log_model_predictions[[model_name]] <- predictions
  log_model_tuning[[model_name]] <- tuning
}

# Check that every model predicted all 29 participants
stopifnot(
  all(sapply(log_model_predictions, function(x) !anyNA(x)))
)
```

```{r}
# Calculate RMSE and R2 using log-transformed outcome
evaluate_log_model <- function(predicted) {

  c(
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((y_log - predicted)^2)),

    R2 = 1 -
      sum((y_log - predicted)^2) /
      sum((y_log - mean(y_log))^2)
  )
}

log_model_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(log_model_predictions, evaluate_log_model)
)

log_model_results <- data.frame(
  Model = names(log_model_predictions),
  log_model_results,
  row.names = NULL
)

log_model_results

table(log_model_tuning[["Gene expression"]]$Lambda)
table(log_model_tuning[["Gene expression"]]$Alpha)
```

```{r}
# Standardize RMSE using the SD of the log-transformed outcome
sd_log_outcome <- sd(y_log)

log_model_results$Standardized_RMSE <-
  log_model_results$RMSE / sd_log_outcome

log_model_results
```

#### individuals with highest error analysis:

```{r}
#### Individuals with highest error

# Create participant-level squared errors for the main model
error_df <- tibble(
  participant_id = analysis_tpm$participant_id,
  observed_log = y_log,
  predicted_log = log_model_predictions[["Gene expression"]],
  squared_error = (y_log - log_model_predictions[["Gene expression"]])^2
) %>%
  arrange(desc(squared_error)) %>%
  mutate(
    rank = row_number(),
    top3 = rank <= 3
  )

# Percent of total squared error from the top 3 participants
top3_percent <- 100 * sum(error_df$squared_error[1:3]) / sum(error_df$squared_error)
top3_percent

# Plot for appendix
error_plot <- ggplot(error_df, aes(
  x = reorder(participant_id, squared_error),
  y = squared_error,
  fill = top3
)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey75", "TRUE" = "firebrick")) +
  labs(
    title = "Participant-level squared prediction errors",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Top 3 participants account for ",
      round(top3_percent, 1),
      "% of total squared error"
    ),
    x = "Participant ID",
    y = "Squared prediction error",
    fill = "Top 3 error"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
```

### Try 0 imputation for vaccination (on log-transformed data)

```{r}
# =========================================================
# Sensitivity analysis: Zero imputation of vaccination history
# Log-transformed outcome, n = 29
# =========================================================

# Store predictions and selected hyperparameters
zero_vax_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_log))

zero_vax_alphas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
zero_vax_lambdas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))

for (i in seq_along(folds)) {

  cat("Running zero-imputation model - fold", i, "\n")

  test_idx <- folds[[i]]

  # Split predictors and outcome
  X_train <- X_combined[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_combined[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  y_train <- y_log[-test_idx]

  # Extract vaccination history
  vax_train <- vax_count[-test_idx]
  vax_test <- vax_count[test_idx]

  # Replace missing histories with zero
  vax_train[is.na(vax_train)] <- 0
  vax_test[is.na(vax_test)] <- 0

  # Add vaccination history to gene expression + demographics
  X_train <- cbind(X_train, n_prior_vax = vax_train)
  X_test <- cbind(X_test, n_prior_vax = vax_test)

  # Remove zero-variance predictors using training data only
  keep_predictors <- apply(X_train, 2, var) > 0

  X_train <- X_train[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_test[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]

  # Use same inner CV splits as the primary analysis
  set.seed(1000 + i)

  inner_folds <- createFolds(
    y_train,
    k = 5,
    returnTrain = TRUE
  )

  # Fit elastic net
  zero_vax_model <- caret::train(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    method = "glmnet",
    tuneGrid = log_elastic_net_grid,
    trControl = trainControl(
      method = "cv",
      index = inner_folds,
      summaryFunction = rmse_only
    ),
    metric = "RMSE",
    preProcess = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
    standardize = FALSE
  )

  # Predict held-out participants on log scale
  zero_vax_predictions[test_idx] <- as.numeric(
    predict(zero_vax_model, newdata = X_test)
  )

  # Store selected hyperparameters
  zero_vax_alphas[i] <- zero_vax_model$bestTune$alpha
  zero_vax_lambdas[i] <- zero_vax_model$bestTune$lambda
}

stopifnot(!anyNA(zero_vax_predictions))
```

```{r}
# Median-imputation predictions from primary analysis

# Function to calculate performance on log scale
evaluate_log <- function(predicted) {
  c(
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((y_log - predicted)^2)),
    R2 = 1 - sum((y_log - predicted)^2) /
      sum((y_log - mean(y_log))^2),
    Standardized_RMSE =
      sqrt(mean((y_log - predicted)^2)) / sd(y_log)
  )
}

# Compare models

  "Genes + age + sex" =
    evaluate_log(
      log_model_predictions[["Genes + age + sex"]]
    ),

  "Median imputation" =
    evaluate_log(median_vax_predictions),

  "Zero imputation" =
    evaluate_log(zero_vax_predictions)
)
```

```{r}
# Evaluate on the LOG-TRANSFORMED outcome scale
evaluate_loocv <- function(predicted) {

  rmse <- sqrt(mean((y_log - predicted)^2))

  c(
    RMSE = rmse,
    R2 = 1 -
      sum((y_log - predicted)^2) /
      sum((y_log - mean(y_log))^2),
    Standardized_RMSE = rmse / sd(y_log)
  )
}

loocv_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(loocv_predictions, evaluate_loocv)
)

loocv_results <- data.frame(
  Model = names(loocv_predictions),
  loocv_results,
  row.names = NULL
)
```

#### check if a few participants are driving the error

```{r}
# Compare participant-level prediction errors
loocv_diagnostics <- data.frame(
  participant_id = analysis_tpm$participant_id,
  observed = y_log,
  baseline = loocv_predictions[["Training-mean baseline"]],
  gene_predicted = loocv_predictions[["Gene expression"]],
  combined_predicted = loocv_predictions[["Genes + age + sex"]]
) %>%
  mutate(
    gene_squared_error = (observed - gene_predicted)^2,
    baseline_squared_error = (observed - baseline)^2
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(gene_squared_error))

# Largest prediction errors
head(loocv_diagnostics, 10)

# Percentage of total error from the three largest errors
100 * sum(head(loocv_diagnostics$gene_squared_error, 3)) /
  sum(loocv_diagnostics$gene_squared_error)
```

```{r}
# Compare individual LOOCV errors and tuning parameters

loocv_error_check <- data.frame(
  participant_id = analysis_tpm$participant_id,
  observed_log = y_log,
  baseline_pred = loocv_predictions[["Training-mean baseline"]],
  gene_pred = loocv_predictions[["Gene expression"]],
  alpha = loocv_tuning[["Gene expression"]]$Alpha,
  lambda = loocv_tuning[["Gene expression"]]$Lambda
) %>%
  mutate(
    baseline_squared_error = (observed_log - baseline_pred)^2,
    gene_squared_error = (observed_log - gene_pred)^2,
    extra_squared_error =
      gene_squared_error - baseline_squared_error
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(extra_squared_error))

# Show participants for whom elastic net performed
# most poorly relative to the training-mean baseline
loocv_error_check %>%
  select(
    participant_id,
    observed_log,
    baseline_pred,
    gene_pred,
    alpha,
    lambda,
    extra_squared_error
  ) %>%
  head(10)
```

```{r}
loocv_error_check %>%
  mutate(
    prediction_shift = gene_pred - baseline_pred
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(prediction_shift))) %>%
  select(
    participant_id,
    observed_log,
    baseline_pred,
    gene_pred,
    alpha,
    lambda,
    prediction_shift
  ) %>%
  head(10)
```

```{r}
# Check how unusual each participant's gene-expression profile is

expression_distance <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(X_mat)), function(i) {

  X_train <- X_mat[-i, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_mat[i, ]

  # Standardize using training data only
  train_mean <- colMeans(X_train)
  train_sd <- apply(X_train, 2, sd)

  # Exclude genes without variability
  keep <- train_sd > 0

  # Mean absolute standardized difference
  mean(abs(
    (X_test[keep] - train_mean[keep]) / train_sd[keep]
  ))
})

expression_diagnostics <- data.frame(
  participant_id = analysis_tpm$participant_id,
  expression_distance = expression_distance,
  loocv_error = (
    y_log - loocv_predictions[["Gene expression"]]
  )^2
)

expression_diagnostics %>%
  arrange(desc(loocv_error)) %>%
  head(10)
```
